models.name: brz_customers
models.description: Faithful mapping of the application customer source.

output.sql: SELECT c.id AS "id", c.first_name AS "first_name", c.last_name AS "last_name" FROM "source"."jaffle_shop"."customers" AS "c"

models.name: brz_orders
models.description: Faithful mapping of application orders without invented order amounts.

output.sql: SELECT o.id AS "id", o.user_id AS "user_id", o.order_date AS "order_date", o.status AS "status" FROM "source"."jaffle_shop"."orders" AS "o"

models.name: brz_payments
models.description: Preserve original payment amounts in cents.

output.sql: SELECT p.id AS "id", p.order_id AS "order_id", p.payment_method AS "payment_method", p.amount AS "amount" FROM "source"."jaffle_shop"."payments" AS "p"

models.name: gld_customer_cohorts
models.description: Disjoint customer cohorts using raw CTEs, INTERSECT, EXCEPT and UNION.

output.sql: WITH completed AS (SELECT o.customer_id FROM ref.slv_orders AS o WHERE o.status = 'completed'), returned AS (SELECT o.customer_id FROM ref.slv_orders AS o WHERE o.status = 'returned'), both_statuses AS (SELECT c.customer_id FROM completed AS c INTERSECT SELECT r.customer_id FROM returned AS r), completed_only AS (SELECT c.customer_id FROM completed AS c EXCEPT SELECT r.customer_id FROM returned AS r) SELECT c.customer_id, 'completed_only' AS cohort FROM completed_only AS c UNION SELECT b.customer_id, 'completed_and_returned' AS cohort FROM both_statuses AS b

models.name: gld_join_counts
models.description: Compare structured inner, left, right, full and cross joins between orders and customers.

steps.name: cross_rows
steps.sql: SELECT 'cross' AS "join_type", COUNT(*) AS "row_count" FROM "ref"."slv_orders" AS "o" CROSS JOIN "ref"."slv_customers" AS "c"

steps.name: full_rows
steps.sql: SELECT 'full' AS "join_type", COUNT(*) AS "row_count" FROM "ref"."slv_orders" AS "o" FULL JOIN "ref"."slv_customers" AS "c" ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id

steps.name: inner_rows
steps.sql: SELECT 'inner' AS "join_type", COUNT(*) AS "row_count" FROM "ref"."slv_orders" AS "o" INNER JOIN "ref"."slv_customers" AS "c" ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id

steps.name: left_rows
steps.sql: SELECT 'left' AS "join_type", COUNT(*) AS "row_count" FROM "ref"."slv_orders" AS "o" LEFT JOIN "ref"."slv_customers" AS "c" ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id

steps.name: right_rows
steps.sql: SELECT 'right' AS "join_type", COUNT(*) AS "row_count" FROM "ref"."slv_orders" AS "o" RIGHT JOIN "ref"."slv_customers" AS "c" ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id

output.sql: SELECT i.join_type, i.row_count FROM step.inner_rows AS i UNION ALL SELECT l.join_type, l.row_count FROM step.left_rows AS l UNION ALL SELECT r.join_type, r.row_count FROM step.right_rows AS r UNION ALL SELECT f.join_type, f.row_count FROM step.full_rows AS f UNION ALL SELECT c.join_type, c.row_count FROM step.cross_rows AS c

models.name: gld_macro_arguments
models.description: Macro defaults, positional/named arguments, arrays, DuckDB maps and a nested wrapper.

output.sql: SELECT o.order_id AS "order_id", ROUND(o.amount, 2) AS "default_rounding", ROUND(o.amount, 1) AS "positional_rounding", ROUND(o.amount, 1) AS "named_rounding", ROUND(o.amount, 1) AS "alternate_named_rounding", ROUND(COALESCE(o.amount, 0) + 1, 1) AS "rounded_with_fee" FROM "ref"."gld_orders" AS "o"

columns.name: rounded_with_fee
columns.description: Add a fictional one-unit fee to demonstrate array/map macro arguments; not used by the marts.

models.name: gld_customer_attribute_hash
models.description: Adapter introspection deferred to dbt; offline inspect/optimize reject this runtime-only model.

output.sql: SELECT c.customer_id AS "customer_id", HASH_RELATION_ATTRIBUTES(ref.slv_customers, table_alias => 'c', exclude => ['customer_id']) AS "attribute_hash" FROM "ref"."slv_customers" AS "c"

models.name: gld_customers
models.description: Classic Jaffle Shop customer mart; all customers retained, all order statuses counted.

steps.name: customer_orders
steps.sql: SELECT o.customer_id AS "customer_id", MIN(o.order_date) AS "first_order", MAX(o.order_date) AS "most_recent_order", COUNT(*) AS "number_of_orders", CAST(SUM(o.amount) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "customer_lifetime_value" FROM "ref"."gld_orders" AS "o" GROUP BY o.customer_id

output.sql: SELECT c.customer_id AS "customer_id", c.first_name AS "first_name", c.last_name AS "last_name", o.first_order AS "first_order", o.most_recent_order AS "most_recent_order", COALESCE(o.number_of_orders, CAST(0 AS BIGINT)) AS "number_of_orders", CAST(COALESCE(o.customer_lifetime_value, 0) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "customer_lifetime_value" FROM "ref"."slv_customers" AS "c" LEFT JOIN "step"."customer_orders" AS "o" ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id

columns.name: customer_lifetime_value
columns.description: Sum of all order payments, matching the classic demo; no refund ledger is supplied.

models.name: gld_daily_sales
models.description: Daily order and payment totals split by lifecycle status, not net recognized revenue.

output.sql: SELECT o.order_date AS "order_date", o.status AS "status", COUNT(*) AS "order_count", CAST(ROUND(SUM(o.amount), 2) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "payment_total" FROM "ref"."gld_orders" AS "o" GROUP BY o.order_date, o.status

models.name: gld_optimizer_constants
models.description: Source-free constant folding, useful before showing the business examples.

output.sql: SELECT 100 / 100 AS currency_scale, 1 + 2 AS sample_value

models.name: gld_customer_leaderboard
models.description: Inspect one output through DISTINCT, independent aggregation branches, HAVING, joins, ranking and a final limit.

steps.name: customer_activity
steps.sql: SELECT a.customer_id AS "customer_id", COUNT(*) AS "all_order_count", SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'returned' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "returned_order_count" FROM "ref"."slv_orders" AS "a" GROUP BY a.customer_id

columns.name: returned_order_count
columns.expression: SUM(CASE WHEN a.status = 'returned' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

steps.name: completed_orders
steps.sql: SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id AS "order_id", o.customer_id AS "customer_id", ROUND(o.amount, 2) AS "amount" FROM "ref"."gld_orders" AS "o" WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.amount > 0

steps.name: customer_totals
steps.sql: SELECT c.customer_id AS "customer_id", ROUND(SUM(c.amount), 2) AS "revenue", COUNT(*) AS "order_count", MAX(c.amount) AS "largest_order" FROM "step"."completed_orders" AS "c" GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2

steps.name: ranked
steps.sql: WITH scored AS (SELECT t.customer_id, t.revenue, t.order_count, ROUND(t.revenue / NULLIF(t.order_count, 0), 2) AS average_amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY t.revenue DESC, t.customer_id) AS revenue_rank FROM step.customer_totals AS t INNER JOIN step.customer_activity AS a ON t.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE a.all_order_count >= 3) SELECT customer_id, revenue, order_count, average_amount, revenue_rank FROM scored

output.sql: SELECT r.customer_id AS "customer_id", r.revenue AS "ranked_revenue", r.revenue_rank AS "revenue_rank", r.average_amount AS "average_amount", r.order_count AS "order_count" FROM "step"."ranked" AS "r" WHERE r.revenue_rank <= 3 ORDER BY r.revenue_rank, r.customer_id LIMIT 2

columns.name: ranked_revenue
columns.description: Top-two eligible completed-order payment totals, not all-status customer lifetime value.

models.name: gld_customer_lifetime_value
models.description: Teaching input - merge two pass-through steps and fold the added zero without changing totals.

steps.name: projected_orders
steps.sql: SELECT o.customer_id AS "customer_id", o.amount AS "amount", o.status AS "unused_status" FROM "ref"."gld_orders" AS "o"

steps.name: normalized_orders
steps.sql: SELECT p.customer_id AS "customer_id", p.amount + 0 AS "amount" FROM "step"."projected_orders" AS "p"

output.sql: SELECT n.customer_id AS "customer_id", CAST(ROUND(SUM(n.amount), 2) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "lifetime_value" FROM "step"."normalized_orders" AS "n" GROUP BY n.customer_id

columns.name: lifetime_value
columns.description: Total payments for customers with orders; unlike gld_customers, customers without orders are absent.

models.name: gld_customer_order_ranking
models.description: Top two orders per customer; the ranking boundary, tie-breaker and final limit must survive.

output.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.amount DESC, o.order_id) AS position FROM ref.gld_orders AS o) SELECT r.order_id, r.customer_id, r.amount, r.position FROM ranked AS r WHERE r.position <= 2 ORDER BY r.customer_id, r.position LIMIT 10

models.name: gld_distinct_paying_customers
models.description: Keep DISTINCT customer/order pairs before projecting customer_id; a customer can legitimately appear twice.

output.sql: SELECT paid.customer_id FROM (SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id, o.order_id FROM ref.gld_orders AS o WHERE o.amount > 0) AS paid

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: One row per distinct paid customer/order pair, NOT one row per customer.

models.name: gld_high_value_customers
models.description: Orders above the global average having a credit-card payment; scalar and correlated subqueries.

output.sql: SELECT candidate_order.order_id, candidate_order.customer_id, candidate_order.amount, (SELECT AVG(benchmark_order.amount) FROM ref.gld_orders AS benchmark_order) AS average_order_amount FROM ref.gld_orders AS candidate_order WHERE candidate_order.amount > (SELECT AVG(benchmark_order.amount) FROM ref.gld_orders AS benchmark_order) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM ref.slv_payments AS eligible_payment WHERE eligible_payment.order_id = candidate_order.order_id AND eligible_payment.payment_method = 'credit_card')

models.name: gld_payment_union
models.description: UNION ALL of card and non-card payments; repeated order/amount pairs must not be deduplicated.

output.sql: SELECT p.order_id, p.amount FROM ref.slv_payments AS p WHERE p.payment_method = 'credit_card' UNION ALL SELECT p.order_id, p.amount FROM ref.slv_payments AS p WHERE p.payment_method <> 'credit_card'

models.name: gld_orders
models.description: One row per order, with all payment methods aggregated before the join.

steps.name: order_payments
steps.sql: SELECT p.order_id AS "order_id", CAST(SUM(p.amount) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "amount", CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_method = 'credit_card' THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "credit_card_amount", COUNT(*) AS "payment_count" FROM "ref"."slv_payments" AS "p" GROUP BY p.order_id

columns.name: credit_card_amount
columns.expression: CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_method = 'credit_card' THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) AS DECIMAL(12, 2))

output.sql: SELECT o.order_id AS "order_id", o.customer_id AS "customer_id", o.order_date AS "order_date", o.status AS "status", CAST(COALESCE(p.amount, 0) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "amount", CAST(COALESCE(p.credit_card_amount, 0) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "credit_card_amount", COALESCE(p.payment_count, CAST(0 AS BIGINT)) AS "payment_count" FROM "ref"."slv_orders" AS "o" LEFT JOIN "step"."order_payments" AS "p" ON o.order_id = p.order_id

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Total payments for the order, including returned or pending orders; not net revenue.

models.name: gld_payment_method_summary
models.description: Payment-method usage, including zero-value payments.

output.sql: SELECT p.payment_method AS "payment_method", COUNT(*) AS "payment_count", COUNT(DISTINCT p.order_id) AS "paid_order_count", CAST(SUM(p.amount) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "payment_total" FROM "ref"."slv_payments" AS "p" GROUP BY p.payment_method

models.name: slv_customers
models.description: Standardized customer identifiers and names; owns a check-strategy snapshot.

output.sql: SELECT CAST(c.id AS BIGINT) AS "customer_id", TRIM(c.first_name) AS "first_name", TRIM(c.last_name) AS "last_name" FROM "ref"."brz_customers" AS "c"

columns.name: first_name
columns.description: Customer first name, with surrounding whitespace removed.

columns.name: last_name
columns.description: Customer last-name initial, with surrounding whitespace removed.

models.name: slv_orders
models.description: Standardized order keys, date and lifecycle status.

output.sql: SELECT CAST(o.id AS BIGINT) AS "order_id", CAST(o.user_id AS BIGINT) AS "customer_id", CAST(o.order_date AS DATE) AS "order_date", LOWER(TRIM(o.status)) AS "status" FROM "ref"."brz_orders" AS "o"

models.name: slv_payments
models.description: Payments in currency units; shorthand columns deliberately demonstrate enrich.

output.sql: SELECT CAST(p.id AS BIGINT) AS "payment_id", p.order_id AS "order_id", p.payment_method AS "payment_method", CAST(ROUND(p.amount / 100.0, 2) AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS "amount" FROM "ref"."brz_payments" AS "p"

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Payment amount converted from cents to currency units.
